new_statements.rule_in_words: Yuwan has no stress accent; it has a lexical three-pattern (N-kei) pitch accent/word-tone system. Every root belongs to one of three classes whose pitch shape is computed over the phonological word (host + clitics) by mora count: Type I = pitch fall after the penultimate mora (HH…HL), Type II = fall after the syllable containing the second mora from the left (HHLL…), Type III = low throughout with a rise on the final mora (LL…LH). The class is lexical; the location of the pitch event within each class is predictable from the word edges.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described (no stress at all; the only sub-regularity is that words with an initial glottalized resonant or kˀw/kˀj show the Type II fall after the first mora, §2.5.2 p. 51).
new_statements.exceptions: Glottalized-initial words form a phonotactically conditioned subcategory of Type II with the fall after the first mora (p. 51); many tokens are realized with flat pitch so class membership is sometimes indeterminate (p. 52); compounds keep the pattern of the first stem; recent loans via Standard Japanese tend to Type I (p. 52). Of 207 nominals: I 48%, II 27%, III 25%. Niinaga 2010 (pp. 43-44) numbers the same three classes differently (1 = final-mora high, 2 = final-mora low, 3 = fall at the word boundary).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word = grammatical word plus following clitics (§2.1.2, §2.5); Table 20 gives isolation forms and forms with =nu, =n, =gadɨ, showing the fall/rise moving with the clitics. Tone-bearing unit is the mora (long vowels/diphthongs count two morae). Lawrence 2018 (pp. 121 ff.) independently confirms the three-pattern system with c. 800 classified words.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement describes Yuwan (湯湾, Uken village, south-western Amami Ōshima), the variety Glottolog 5.1 uses as the Glottolog's most extensive description for sout2954 and files all Niinaga Yuwan works; Note that in Japanese dialectology 'southern Amami Ōshima' (奄美大島南部) more narrowly means Setouchi town (Koniya, Shodon/Kakeroma etc.); those dialects have a different, TWO-pattern word-tone system (Matsumori 2019 p. 5: '瀬戸内町の諸方言は二型アクセント体系を持つ'; Hayata 1996 p. 23 on Shodon: a word-tone language with phrase-final falling vs rising tones), whereas Yuwan has THREE lexical patterns. Uwano 2000 groups Uken village with Setouchi as the 'southern area' of the island, consistent with Glottolog's assignment. Either way the typological reading is the same: lexical N-pattern pitch accent (word tone), no stress accent.

sources.note: §2.5 'Prosody' (pp. 49-52): Yuwan has lexical prosody with three pitch patterns (I: fall after the penultimate mora of the phonological word; II: fall after the syllable containing the second mora; III: rise on the final mora); tone-bearing unit = mora, domain = phonological word (word + clitics); glottalized-initial words form a phonotactically conditioned subtype of II; 207 nominals: I 48%, II 27%, III 25%; many tokens realized flat; verbs/adjectives have the same patterns; no mention of stress.

sources.note: p. 121: Yuwan is 'a three-pattern tonal (三型音調) dialect, rare on Amami Ōshima'; quotes Niinaga & Ogawa 2011's characterization (I: fall after the syllable containing the 2nd mora from the end of the bunsetsu; II: fall after the syllable containing the 2nd mora from the beginning; III: only the bunsetsu-final mora high) and classifies c. 800 words by pattern I/II/III. Independent fieldwork confirming the three-pattern system.

sources.note: p. 5: '古仁屋方言をはじめとした瀬戸内町の諸方言は二型アクセント体系を持つ' — Koniya and the other Setouchi dialects have a two-pattern accent system: a 'falling type' (2nd mora from the start of the bunsetsu high, phrase ends falling) and a 'rising type' (two H peaks in 3+ mora phrases, phrase ends rising); classes correlate with historical tone series A vs B/C. pitch accent/word-tone, no stress statement. Relevant because Setouchi is the traditional 'southern Amami' area under ISO ams.

sources.note: Survey of Amami accent systems from the author's 200-village fieldwork: N-pattern (mostly two-pattern) accent systems dominate, multi-pattern systems scattered; double-peaked contours concentrate in Kikai and in southern Amami Ōshima (Uken village and Setouchi town); e.g. Shiba (Kakeroma, Setouchi) 'is basically a two-pattern accent system' (p. 44-45). No stress statement; Yuwan not treated individually.
